description: Returns the signals of one ticker or a comma list of up to 50 in the path (a screen's matches, say) over time, all-time: up to 25 signals in `select`, or `*` for every signal the grain stores, every ticker on one shared grid. `series` is keyed by symbol, one flat row per grain step. Paged backward: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` with the same params. For when a yes/no signal flipped, use tickerbot_query_events with kind=signal.

asof.description: Point-in-time read: one result per ticker (the state at that instant) rather than a range. `YYYY-MM-DD` or a full ISO timestamp, the same meaning `asof` carries on `/v2/tickers/{ticker}`, `/v2/scan` and `/v2/signals/{signal}`. Combined with `from`/`to` or `cursor` it is a 400 (a point and a window contradict), and `limit` has no meaning under it. It also resolves which company held the symbol at that instant: a ticker that changed hands returns the state of whoever traded it then, so `/v2/tickers/SHLD/history?asof=2010-06-30` returns Sears Holdings' price and `asof=2026-01-01` returns the Global X defense ETF. Returns the most recent result at or before the instant, so a date inside a trading gap gives the last result before it; on the `1d` and `1w` grids a timestamp returns the previous session's result, never that day's close. Also: `next_cursor` is always `null` (every requested ticker is on the one page). A ticker with no data on the grid at or before the instant (outside the minute tier, say) comes back as an empty array with `_meta.coverage[ticker].rows: 0`; a 404 means only that we do not track the symbol. A bare date on the `1m`/`1h` grid is accepted and means the last result of that day: the ET calendar day for stocks and ETFs, the UTC day for crypto, FX and rates (the state reads 400 that combination; this grid read does not). The look-back is the grid's window: `1d` walks back without limit, `1h` 60 days and `1m` 7 days before the instant. At `grain=1q` a quarter is visible from its `available_at`, when the market could first trade on it: 9:30 AM ET on the report date for a pre-market earnings release, else 9:30 AM ET of the next session; statements the session after filing. A bare date means that day's 4 PM ET close, so you get the latest quarter that was public knowledge at the instant, with restatements after it excluded: `/v2/tickers/AAPL/history?grain=1q&asof=2026-07-30` returns 2026-Q1, `asof=2026-07-31T13:30:00Z` 2026-Q2 (the June quarter was reported after the close on 2026-07-30). See availability. At `grain=1y` a fiscal year is visible from its `available_at`: 9:30 AM ET of the first session after the original annual report was filed. A bare date means that day's 4 PM ET close: `/v2/tickers/AAPL/history?grain=1y&asof=2025-10-31` returns fiscal 2024, `asof=2025-11-03` fiscal 2025 (the 10-K was filed after the close on Friday 2025-10-31). Response time: under 1.5 s cold, under 0.6 s warm.

cursor.description: Continue paging back: the previous response's `next_cursor`, unchanged. Send it with the same params as the first page (`limit` may change); a page whose params differ is a 400 naming the param. On `1m` to `1w` it carries each ticker's own position, so every ticker continues from its own oldest row: nothing is skipped or repeated, even when the tickers trade on different calendars (a stock and a crypto pair). On `1q`/`1y` it carries the shared fiscal label, so every ticker continues from the same period.

from.description: Window start, `YYYY-MM-DD` or ISO: a bare date starts at the beginning of that day, a timestamp is included. At `1q` and `1y` it bounds the fiscal period end. Intraday requests default to a recent window (`1m`: 7 days, `1h`: 60 days); the cursor keeps walking further back window-by-window, or pass `from` to widen it up front.

grain.description: Grid granularity. `1w` resamples the daily grain weekly (Monday-keyed); `1q` is the fiscal-quarter grid; `1y` is the fiscal-year grid of annual statements. This is the grid: there is no `auto` here and nothing blends; under `asof` you get the last result on this grid, and a signal the grid does not carry is a `400`.

limit.description: Grid steps per page. Max 1000; an over-cap `limit` is clamped to 1000. Separately, a page holds at most 25,000 points in all: tickers × `limit` over 25,000 is a 400 (50 tickers take `limit` up to 500; 25 take the full 1,000). With `select=*` the page holds at most 1,000 points: over it, an explicit `limit` is a 400, and the default is lowered to fit (5 tickers get 200).

select.description: Up to 25 signals: built-in signals, your custom signals and OHLCV names, freely mixed. `*` is every signal the grain stores (at `1q` and `1y`, every quarterly or annual field), with no 25-signal cap; its page holds at most 1,000 points (tickers × `limit`), see `limit`. `*` returns the same rows as a named list of stored signals, and its `vwap` is the stored value (a named `vwap` is read from the bars). A name sent beside `*` adds nothing, and an unknown one is a 400. Omitted → the ticker-history default set (price, change_1d_pct, relative_volume, market_cap), intersected with what the grain carries. At `1q`, `select` is required and quarterly-only; at `1y`, required and annual-only (the list is under Notes).

ticker.description: One symbol, or a comma-separated list of up to 50 for a response keyed by symbol, on one aligned grid. A page holds at most 25,000 points in all (tickers × `limit`), so 50 tickers page at up to 500 points each. Case-insensitive. Equities are bare symbols (`NVDA`); every other class carries a prefix: rates (`R:SOFR`), crypto (`X:BTCUSD`), fx (`X:EURUSD`). Bare `BTC`/`ETH` are US-listed ETFs, not spot crypto. See Tickers.

to.description: Window end, `YYYY-MM-DD` or ISO. A bare date covers that whole day. A timestamp is included until 2027-01-12 and exclusive from then, as everywhere else (Deprecations). At `1m`/`1h` a bare date on `from` or `to` is each ticker's market day: the ET calendar day for stocks and ETFs, the UTC day for crypto, FX and rates, ticker by ticker in a mixed list. See Time windows.

name: tickerbot_get_history
